forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred south of the Bight extends a ridge across the south of SA. The main high centre will gradually move eastwards to be centred to the east of SA on Friday. A trough over the interior of WA will remain stationary but will weaken later Friday. Another low pressure trough will approach from the west on Saturday and move across SA on Sunday then a cold front will move across southern coasts later Monday. An upper disturbance will move over the far west on Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning fog about eastern districts. Dry apart from isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures slightly below average in the west and south but above average in the northeast. East to northeasterly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the northeast.
Dry apart from isolated showers and thunderstorms in the northwest and far west. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh at times near the coast and in the north.

Patchy morning fog about the South East districts. Dry apart from the chance of a shower or thunderstorm in the far southwest in the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northerly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the northeast.

text.p: Showers and isolated thunderstorms extending across the west and south. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northwesterly winds, shifting southwest to southeasterly from the west.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Isolated showers developing about southern coastal districts during the afternoon, extending over the remainder of the southern agricultural area in the evening. Maximum temperatures below average about the southern agricultural area but above average elsewhere. Fresh southwest to southeasterly winds extending throughout.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: less than 2 mm about the southern agricultural area, although local falls of 2 to 5 mm are likely about southern coastal districts, possibly reaching 5 to 10 mm about parts of the Lower South East. 5 to 15 mm is likely over areas west of about Ceduna, but local heavier falls of 15 to 30 mm are possible in the far west.
